summary: Arrange repeated 3D views under an explicit comparison contract: shared identity, projection, scale, legend and interaction where those conditions carry the claim.
objective: A viewer can attribute differences to the chosen variable rather than mismatched camera, viewport, normalization, clipping or selection state.
applies_when: Several states, datasets, parameter values or models must be compared simultaneously.
The comparison depends on spatial size, direction, shape or field magnitude.
intent_signals: compare several 3D states at equal scale
linked viewports shared camera scientific comparison
example_prompts: Compare four deformation states with matched orthographic scale, axes and legend.
Show three climate fields in linked panels and disclose any independently normalized range.
negative_signals: Calling panels comparable while silently fitting each camera independently.
Sharing a color palette while using different unmarked domains.
not_for: A before/after toggle where simultaneous panels add no value.
A focus/context inset where the views intentionally have different roles and scales.

principles: Write the comparison contract first: changed variable, fixed conditions and any deliberately independent normalization. Equal apparent size is required only when the claim depends on size.
Link stable entity IDs, selection and probes across panels; decide separately whether camera orientation, zoom, time and clipping are synchronized.
A shared legend is valid only for a shared value mapping. If domains differ, show the mappings beside each panel rather than hiding normalization.
implementation: In Blender, author one reference frame, units, camera candidates and state collections; do not bake panel placement into world coordinates.

In Three.js WebGL, assign logical-pixel viewport/scissor rectangles and enable scissor testing so each camera stays inside its panel. Use one orthographic frustum/zoom or equivalent world-units-per-pixel rule when equal apparent scale is part of the claim; update all projections on resize.
Render shared axes/scale cues and a panel title outside ambiguous 3D depth. Route selection by viewport, then broadcast the stable ID and probe coordinate to linked panels.
observable_checks: A reference segment occupies the same declared screen length across equal-scale panels after resize; a deliberately independent scale is labeled in that panel.
Click the same feature in each panel: linked identity and probe coordinate agree, while the changed variable alone produces the reported difference.
Clear each panel independently and inspect its borders: no draw, pick or label leaks into a neighboring scissor region.

creative_affordances: Use grids, strips, paired lenses or a movable comparison tray according to panel count and task.
Synchronize only the dimensions that aid the comparison; independent orbit may remain available behind a relink action.
known_limits: WebGLRenderer viewport/scissor mechanics do not establish comparison validity or support in other renderer backends.
Orthographic distance-invariant image size does not itself guarantee equal scale when frusta, zoom or viewport sizes differ.
No multi-viewport render, pick, resize or quantitative comparison was run.

claims.statement: Three.js WebGLRenderer setViewport defines a render viewport in logical pixels, setScissor defines a region, and enabled scissor testing limits affected pixels to that region.
claims.scope: WebGL mechanism only; panel layout, clearing, picking and synchronization are application responsibilities.

claims.statement: Three.js OrthographicCamera documents that an object’s rendered size stays constant regardless of camera distance, with scale controlled by frustum planes and zoom and projection updates required after changes.
claims.scope: Projection property only; matched panel scale still requires matching frustum/zoom and viewport conventions.

source_refs.locator: Class description; frustum planes; zoom; updateProjectionMatrix
